page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-8-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance from the c4 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz. This x86_64 architecture server features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 62.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes a 504 MB L3 cache and a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD, while offering zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a mix of performance characteristics. The instance demonstrates top-tier performance in Geekbench text processing, scoring 2924.0, and strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 35.4 GB/sec. It also achieves strong text generation speeds of 283.92 tokens/sec for small 135M parameter LLM models. However, there are notable memory performance tradeoffs: the Passmark memory score is weak, and the uncached read-only memory bandwidth for large blocks is limited to 39.24 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Conversely, cached small-block read-only memory bandwidth is average at 691.79 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-8-lssd offers a dense allocation of memory and local NVMe storage relative to its 8 vCPUs, making it a viable option for workloads requiring fast local scratch space without the overhead of external storage. The inclusion of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions supports specialized vector and matrix operations. This server is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, text processing pipelines, and small-scale language model inference, though its lower uncached memory bandwidth should be factored into memory-bound application designs.
